name: Entropy H(X)
type_signature: discrete RV X with pmf p → R_{≥0}
description: The expected value −Σ p(x) log p(x) of the self-information of a discrete random variable, measuring its average uncertainty in bits.
_deps: discrete probability mass function, logarithm base 2

name: Joint entropy H(X,Y)
description: The entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(x,y) of a pair of random variables treated as a single vector-valued variable.
_deps: joint probability mass function, entropy

name: Conditional entropy H(Y|X)
description: The expected entropy −ΣΣ p(x,y) log p(y|x) of Y averaged over the conditioning variable X.
_deps: conditional pmf, joint pmf, entropy

name: Mutual information I(X;Y)
description: The relative entropy D(p(x,y)‖p(x)p(y)) between the joint distribution and the product of marginals, equal to H(X)−H(X|Y).
_deps: joint and marginal distributions, relative entropy, entropy

name: Conditional mutual information I(X;Y|Z)
description: The expected reduction in uncertainty about X from knowing Y, given Z, equal to H(X|Z)−H(X|Y,Z).
_deps: conditional entropy, mutual information

name: Mutual information–entropy relations
description: The identities I(X;Y)=H(X)−H(X|Y)=H(Y)−H(Y|X)=H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y) and I(X;X)=H(X).
_deps: entropy, conditional entropy, joint entropy, mutual information

name: Chain rule for entropy
description: The joint entropy decomposes as H(X_1,...,X_n)=Σ_i H(X_i | X_{i−1},...,X_1).
_deps: conditional entropy, joint entropy

name: Chain rule for mutual information
description: The mutual information decomposes as I(X_1,...,X_n; Y)=Σ_i I(X_i; Y | X_{i−1},...,X_1).
_deps: conditional mutual information

name: Chain rule for relative entropy
description: The joint relative entropy decomposes as D(p(x,y)‖q(x,y))=D(p(x)‖q(x))+D(p(y|x)‖q(y|x)).
_deps: relative entropy, conditional relative entropy

name: Information inequality (Gibbs' inequality)
description: Relative entropy is nonnegative, D(p‖q) ≥ 0, with equality if and only if p=q.
_deps: relative entropy, Jensen's inequality

name: Nonnegativity of mutual information
description: I(X;Y) ≥ 0 with equality if and only if X and Y are independent.
_deps: information inequality, mutual information as relative entropy

name: Conditioning reduces entropy
description: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X), with equality iff X and Y are independent; conditioning never increases entropy on average.
_deps: nonnegativity of mutual information

name: Uniform distribution maximizes entropy
description: For a finite alphabet of size m, H(X) ≤ log m with equality iff X is uniformly distributed.
_deps: information inequality, relative entropy to uniform

name: Independence bound on entropy
description: H(X_1,...,X_n) ≤ Σ_i H(X_i), with equality iff the X_i are mutually independent.
_deps: chain rule for entropy, conditioning reduces entropy

name: Log-sum inequality
description: For nonnegative a_i, b_i, Σ a_i log(a_i/b_i) ≥ (Σ a_i) log((Σ a_i)/(Σ b_i)), with equality iff a_i/b_i is constant.
_deps: convexity of t log t, Jensen's inequality

name: Convexity of relative entropy
description: D(p‖q) is jointly convex in the pair (p,q).
_deps: log-sum inequality

name: Concavity of entropy
description: H(p) is a concave function of the probability distribution p.
_deps: relative entropy, convexity of relative entropy

name: Concavity/convexity of mutual information
description: For fixed p(y|x), I(X;Y) is concave in p(x); for fixed p(x), I(X;Y) is convex in p(y|x).
_deps: mutual information, concavity of entropy, convexity of relative entropy

name: Data-processing inequality
description: If X→Y→Z form a Markov chain then I(X;Y) ≥ I(X;Z); no processing of Y can increase its information about X.
_deps: Markov chain, chain rule for mutual information, nonnegativity of mutual information

name: Fano's inequality
description: For an estimate X̂ of X from Y with error probability P_e, H(P_e)+P_e log(|X|−1) ≥ H(X|Y), lower-bounding the error probability by the conditional entropy.
_deps: conditional entropy, binary entropy function, estimator X→Y→X̂

name: L1 bound on entropy difference
description: If the L1 distance between two distributions p and q on an alphabet of size m is at most 1/2, then |H(p)−H(q)| ≤ −‖p−q‖_1 log(‖p−q‖_1/m).
_deps: entropy, total variation distance

name: Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP)
description: For i.i.d. X_1,...,X_n ~ p, −(1/n) log p(X_1,...,X_n) → H(X) in probability.
_deps: weak law of large numbers, i.i.d. source, entropy

name: Typical set A_ε^{(n)}
description: The set of sequences whose empirical entropy rate −(1/n) log p(x^n) is within ε of H(X), i.e. whose probability is near 2^{−nH}.
_deps: AEP, entropy

name: Properties of the typical set
description: The typical set has probability near 1, has at most 2^{n(H+ε)} elements, at least (1−ε)2^{n(H−ε)} elements, and each member has probability near 2^{−nH}.
_deps: typical set, AEP

name: AEP-based source coding bound
description: i.i.d. sequences can be encoded with about nH(X) bits using roughly n(H+ε) bits per typical sequence and a negligible-probability overflow code.
_deps: typical set properties, source coding

name: Smallest high-probability set B_δ^{(n)}
description: A minimum-cardinality set carrying probability at least 1−δ, whose size to first order in the exponent equals that of the typical set (≈ 2^{nH}).
_deps: typical set, AEP

name: Entropy rate H(𝒳)
description: The per-symbol limit H(𝒳)=lim_{n→∞} (1/n) H(X_1,...,X_n) of the entropy of a stationary stochastic process.
_deps: stationary process, joint entropy, limit

name: Equivalence of entropy-rate definitions
description: For a stationary process the limit H'=lim H(X_n | X_{n−1},...,X_1) exists and equals the entropy rate H(𝒳).
_deps: stationarity, Cesàro mean, conditioning reduces entropy

name: Entropy rate of a Markov chain
description: For a stationary Markov chain with stationary distribution μ and transition matrix P, the entropy rate is H(𝒳)=−Σ_{ij} μ_i P_{ij} log P_{ij}.
_deps: entropy rate, stationary distribution, Markov chain

name: Entropy rate of a hidden Markov / functions of Markov chains
description: For a function Y_i=φ(X_i) of a stationary Markov chain, the entropy rate is squeezed between H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1,X_1) and H(Y_n|Y_{n−1},...,Y_1), both converging to it.
_deps: entropy rate, Markov chain, functions of a process

name: Markov chains and the second law
description: For a Markov chain, relative entropy D(μ_n‖μ'_n) to any other distribution evolving under the same transition decreases with time, and H(X_n) increases toward stationarity for a doubly stochastic chain.
_deps: relative entropy, Markov chain, data-processing

name: Prefix (instantaneous) code
description: A code in which no codeword is a prefix of any other, so each symbol is decodable as soon as its codeword ends.
_deps: variable-length code, codeword alphabet

name: Entropy bound on expected codeword length
description: The expected length L of any prefix D-ary code satisfies L ≥ H_D(X), with equality iff the lengths are l_i=−log_D p_i.
_deps: Kraft inequality, relative entropy, optimal code

name: Shannon code lengths
description: The codeword-length assignment l_i=⌈log(1/p_i)⌉ which satisfies Kraft and achieves expected length within one bit of entropy.
_deps: Kraft inequality, entropy bound on codeword length

name: Optimal code length bound (H ≤ L < H+1)
description: The minimum expected length L* of a prefix code satisfies H_D(X) ≤ L* < H_D(X)+1, and block coding drives the per-symbol length to the entropy rate.
_deps: Shannon code, entropy bound, block coding

name: Penalty for using the wrong code
description: Using a code optimal for q to encode a source p costs an extra D(p‖q) bits per symbol over the entropy, i.e. expected length is between H(p)+D(p‖q) and H(p)+D(p‖q)+1.
_deps: relative entropy, Shannon code, entropy

name: Huffman coding
description: A bottom-up algorithm that builds an optimal prefix code by repeatedly merging the least probable symbols into a combined symbol.
_deps: prefix code, Kraft inequality, expected length minimization

name: Optimality of Huffman codes
description: The Huffman code achieves the minimum expected codeword length over all prefix (hence all uniquely decodable) codes for a given source.
_deps: Huffman coding, properties of optimal codes, Kraft–McMillan

name: Shannon–Fano–Elias coding
description: A coding scheme using the rounded cumulative distribution function F̄(x) truncated to ⌈log(1/p(x))⌉+1 bits to assign prefix-free codewords.
_deps: cumulative distribution function, prefix code, Kraft inequality

name: Arithmetic coding
description: A coding technique that represents an entire sequence by an interval of the unit line determined by cumulative probabilities, encoded by a single number.
_deps: Shannon–Fano–Elias coding, cumulative distribution, sequential model

name: Competitive optimality of Shannon code
description: For Shannon code lengths l(x), no other uniquely decodable code l'(x) can satisfy l'(x) < l(x)−c with probability exceeding 2^{−c+1}; the Shannon code is essentially uncrushable.
_deps: Shannon code, Kraft inequality, dyadic distributions

name: Horse race / gambling model
type_signature: outcomes with probabilities p_i and odds o_i
description: A repeated investment model in which a gambler distributes wealth across m outcomes with win probabilities p_i and payoff odds o_i.
_deps: probability distribution, betting proportions, odds

name: Doubling rate W(b,p)
description: The expected logarithmic growth rate W(b,p)=Σ p_i log(b_i o_i) of wealth per race under bet allocation b.
_deps: horse race, expected log wealth

name: Kelly (proportional) gambling optimality
description: The doubling rate is maximized by proportional betting b_i=p_i, yielding optimal doubling rate W*(p)=Σ p_i log o_i − H(p).
_deps: doubling rate, Jensen / Kuhn–Tucker, horse race

name: Conservation theorem (gambling)
description: For uniform fair odds o_i=m, the sum of the doubling rate and the entropy is constant: W*(p)+H(p)=log m.
_deps: Kelly optimality, entropy, fair odds

name: Value of side information in gambling
description: The increase ΔW in doubling rate due to side information Y equals the mutual information I(X;Y) between the horse race outcome and the side information.
_deps: doubling rate, mutual information, Kelly betting

name: Doubling rate of dependent horse races
description: For a sequence of races, the growth-rate-optimal wealth grows as 2^{nW*} where the per-race doubling rate relates to the entropy rate via W*=Σ log o − H(𝒳) for fair uniform odds.
_deps: doubling rate, entropy rate, gambling estimate of entropy

name: Entropy of English
description: The estimated entropy rate of English (about 1.3 bits/letter) obtained via models and Shannon's guessing/gambling estimation games.
_deps: entropy rate, stochastic model of language, gambling estimate

name: Discrete memoryless channel (DMC)
type_signature: (input alphabet X, transition p(y|x), output alphabet Y)
description: A channel specified by a conditional distribution p(y|x) that acts independently on each transmitted symbol.
_deps: transition probability, input/output alphabets, memorylessness

name: Channel capacity C
description: The maximum mutual information C=max_{p(x)} I(X;Y) over input distributions, the information capacity of the channel.
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, mutual information, maximization over input pmf

name: Binary symmetric channel (BSC)
description: A binary-input binary-output channel that flips each bit independently with probability p, having capacity 1−H(p).
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, binary entropy function

name: Binary erasure channel (BEC)
description: A binary-input channel that erases each symbol with probability α and otherwise transmits it correctly, having capacity 1−α.
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, erasure symbol

name: Symmetric and weakly symmetric channels
type_signature: channel with permuted rows/columns of transition matrix
description: A channel whose transition-matrix rows are permutations of one another (and columns sums equal), for which capacity equals log|Y|−H(row) achieved by the uniform input.
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, channel capacity, uniform input

name: Jointly typical set A_ε^{(n)}
description: The set of pairs (x^n,y^n) that are individually typical and whose joint empirical entropy is near H(X,Y).
_deps: typical set, joint entropy, AEP

name: Joint AEP
description: Jointly typical pairs have probability near 1, number about 2^{nH(X,Y)}, and an independently drawn pair is jointly typical with probability about 2^{−nI(X;Y)}.
_deps: jointly typical set, AEP, mutual information

name: Channel code (M, n)
description: An encoding of M messages into length-n channel inputs together with a decoding rule, with rate R=(log M)/n bits per channel use.
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, encoder, decoder, rate

name: Channel coding theorem (achievability)
description: For any rate R < C there exist codes with maximal error probability tending to 0; all rates below capacity are achievable.
_deps: channel capacity, joint AEP, random coding, jointly typical decoding

name: Converse to the channel coding theorem
description: Any sequence of (2^{nR},n) codes with error probability tending to 0 must have R ≤ C; capacity is the supremum of achievable rates.
_deps: Fano's inequality, data-processing inequality, channel capacity

name: Random coding argument
description: A proof method that generates a codebook at random from p(x), bounds the expected error probability, and concludes a good code exists.
_deps: jointly typical decoding, joint AEP, expectation argument

name: Jointly typical decoding
description: A decoder that declares the unique codeword jointly typical with the received sequence, erring only on atypicality or collision.
_deps: jointly typical set, joint AEP

name: Feedback capacity theorem
description: Feedback does not increase the capacity of a discrete memoryless channel: C_FB=C.
_deps: channel capacity, converse, data-processing

name: Source–channel separation theorem
description: A source of entropy rate H can be transmitted reliably over a channel of capacity C iff H < C, and separate optimal source and channel coding is asymptotically optimal.
_deps: channel coding theorem, AEP source coding, Fano's inequality

name: Zero-error capacity
description: The largest rate at which messages can be sent over a channel with exactly zero probability of error, related to the independence number of the channel's confusability graph.
_deps: discrete memoryless channel, combinatorial confusability graph

name: Differential entropy h(X)
type_signature: continuous RV with density f → R ∪ {±∞}
description: The quantity h(X)=−∫ f(x) log f(x) dx, the continuous analogue of entropy for a random variable with density f.
_deps: probability density function, integral, logarithm

name: Differential entropy of uniform and Gaussian
description: The uniform on [0,a] has differential entropy log a, and the N(0,σ²) Gaussian has differential entropy (1/2) log(2πeσ²).
_deps: differential entropy, uniform/normal density

name: AEP for differential entropy
description: For i.i.d. continuous X_i with density f, −(1/n) log f(X^n) → h(X), and the typical set has volume about 2^{nh(X)}.
_deps: AEP, differential entropy, weak law of large numbers

name: Relation of differential to discrete entropy
description: The entropy of an n-bit quantization of a continuous X satisfies H(X^{Δ}) ≈ h(X)+n, so differential entropy is discrete entropy minus the log of the quantization step.
_deps: differential entropy, quantization, Riemann integral

name: Joint and conditional differential entropy
description: The differential entropies h(X,Y)=−∫ f log f and h(X|Y)=h(X,Y)−h(Y) defined for jointly continuous variables.
_deps: differential entropy, joint density

name: Continuous relative entropy and mutual information
description: The relative entropy D(f‖g)=∫ f log(f/g) and mutual information I(X;Y)=h(X)−h(X|Y) for continuous variables, both nonnegative.
_deps: differential entropy, density, information inequality

name: Entropy of the multivariate Gaussian
description: A multivariate normal with covariance K has differential entropy (1/2) log((2πe)^n |K|).
_deps: differential entropy, covariance matrix, determinant

name: Gaussian maximizes differential entropy
description: Among all densities with a given covariance K, the multivariate Gaussian uniquely maximizes differential entropy.
_deps: differential entropy, relative entropy to Gaussian, covariance constraint

name: Hadamard's inequality (via entropy)
description: For a positive-definite covariance matrix K, |K| ≤ Π K_{ii}, derived from the independence bound on differential entropy.
_deps: multivariate Gaussian entropy, independence bound on entropy

name: Gaussian channel
description: A continuous channel adding independent Gaussian noise of power N to the input, typically under an input power constraint E[X²] ≤ P.
_deps: continuous channel, Gaussian noise, power constraint

name: Capacity of the Gaussian channel
description: The power-constrained Gaussian channel has capacity C=(1/2) log(1+P/N) bits per transmission, achieved by Gaussian inputs.
_deps: Gaussian channel, channel capacity, Gaussian maximizes entropy

name: Sphere-packing argument
function_signature: (power P, noise N, n) → (number of distinguishable codewords)
description: A geometric heuristic counting how many noise spheres of radius √(nN) pack into a signal sphere of radius √(n(P+N)), yielding 2^{nC} codewords.
_deps: Gaussian channel, volume of n-sphere, capacity

name: Capacity of the band-limited Gaussian channel
description: A band-limited channel of bandwidth W with power P and noise spectral density N_0/2 has capacity W log(1+P/(N_0 W)) bits per second.
_deps: Gaussian channel capacity, Nyquist sampling theorem, bandwidth

name: Parallel Gaussian channels capacity
description: For k independent Gaussian channels under a total power constraint, capacity is Σ (1/2) log(1+P_i/N_i) maximized over a power allocation summing to P.
_deps: Gaussian channel capacity, Lagrange optimization, power allocation

name: Water-filling power allocation
function_signature: (noise levels N_i, total power P) → (optimal powers P_i)
description: The optimal allocation P_i=(ν−N_i)^+ that pours power into the lowest-noise channels up to a common water level ν.
_deps: parallel Gaussian channels, Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions

name: Capacity with colored Gaussian noise
description: For a Gaussian channel with non-white noise of covariance K_Z, capacity is obtained by water-filling over the eigenvalues of the noise covariance under a power constraint.
_deps: parallel Gaussian channels, water-filling, eigendecomposition of covariance

name: Gaussian channel with feedback
description: For the colored Gaussian channel feedback increases capacity by at most half a bit and at most a factor of two; for the memoryless (white) Gaussian channel feedback does not increase capacity.
_deps: Gaussian channel capacity, feedback, covariance optimization

name: Rate-distortion function R(D)
type_signature: (source p(x), distortion d, level D) → R_{≥0}
description: The minimum mutual information R(D)=min_{p(x̂|x): E d(X,X̂) ≤ D} I(X;X̂) needed to describe a source within average distortion D.
_deps: distortion measure, mutual information, source distribution

name: Distortion measure d(x,x̂)
description: A nonnegative function quantifying the cost of representing source symbol x by reconstruction x̂ (e.g. Hamming or squared-error).
_deps: source and reconstruction alphabets

name: Rate-distortion theorem
description: The operational rate-distortion function (minimum rate for distortion ≤ D) equals the information rate-distortion function R(D)=min I(X;X̂).
_deps: rate-distortion function, joint AEP, random coding, converse

name: Rate-distortion of a Bernoulli source
description: A Bernoulli(p) source under Hamming distortion has R(D)=H(p)−H(D) for 0 ≤ D ≤ min(p,1−p) and 0 beyond.
_deps: rate-distortion function, binary entropy, Hamming distortion

name: Rate-distortion of a Gaussian source
description: A N(0,σ²) source under squared-error distortion has R(D)=(1/2) log(σ²/D) for D ≤ σ² and 0 for D ≥ σ².
_deps: rate-distortion function, differential entropy, squared-error distortion

name: Rate-distortion for parallel Gaussian sources (reverse water-filling)
description: For independent Gaussian sources under total squared-error distortion, the optimal distortion allocation D_i=min(λ,σ_i²) gives reverse water-filling, allocating no rate to low-variance components.
_deps: Gaussian rate-distortion, Lagrange optimization, water-filling

name: Convexity and monotonicity of R(D)
description: The rate-distortion function R(D) is a nonincreasing convex function of the distortion level D.
_deps: rate-distortion function, convexity of mutual information

name: Blahut–Arimoto algorithm
description: An alternating-minimization iteration that computes channel capacity or the rate-distortion function by treating them as a double minimization over two distributions.
_deps: channel capacity, rate-distortion function, alternating optimization, relative entropy

name: Capacity / R(D) as double optimization
description: Both channel capacity and the rate-distortion function can be written as a minimization of relative entropy over two distributions, justifying the Blahut–Arimoto alternating scheme.
_deps: relative entropy, channel capacity, rate-distortion function

name: Strong typicality / method of types (preview)
description: Sequences classified by their empirical type (histogram) so that the probability of a type and the number of sequences of a type are governed by entropy and relative entropy exponents.
_deps: empirical distribution, entropy, relative entropy

name: Binary entropy function H(p)
description: The entropy −p log p −(1−p) log(1−p) of a Bernoulli(p) variable, a concave function peaking at p=1/2.
_deps: entropy, Bernoulli distribution

name: Type (empirical distribution) of a sequence
type_signature: x^n in X^n → P_{x^n} on X
description: The empirical probability distribution P_{x^n} of a length-n sequence, recording the relative frequency of each symbol of the alphabet.

name: Polynomial bound on the number of types
description: The number of distinct types of length-n sequences over an alphabet of size |X| is at most (n+1)^{|X|}, polynomial in n.

name: Method of types
function_signature: (i.i.d. sequence problem) → (combinatorial count over type classes)
description: A combinatorial proof technique that partitions sequences by their type and replaces probability calculations with counting over the polynomially many type classes.

name: Probability of a sequence under Q in terms of type
description: Under i.i.d. distribution Q, the probability of a sequence of type P equals 2^{-n(H(P)+D(P||Q))}, depending on the sequence only through its type.

name: Size of a type class
description: The number of sequences of type P satisfies (n+1)^{-|X|} 2^{nH(P)} ≤ |T(P)| ≤ 2^{nH(P)}, so to first order |T(P)| ≈ 2^{nH(P)}.

name: Probability of a type class under Q
description: Under i.i.d. Q the probability of type class T(P) satisfies (n+1)^{-|X|}2^{-nD(P||Q)} ≤ Q^n(T(P)) ≤ 2^{-nD(P||Q)}, decaying like 2^{-nD(P||Q)}.

name: Universal source code via types
description: A fixed-rate block code that encodes all sequences whose type has entropy below the rate R, achieving asymptotically optimal compression without knowing the source distribution.

name: I-projection (relative-entropy projection)
type_signature: (distribution Q, convex set E) → P* in E
description: The distribution P* in a set E minimizing the relative entropy D(P||Q), the closest distribution in E to Q in the Kullback–Leibler sense.

name: Conditional limit theorem
description: Conditioned on the empirical distribution lying in a convex set E, the marginal distribution of a single coordinate converges to the I-projection P* of Q onto E.

name: Pythagorean theorem for relative entropy
description: For the I-projection P* of Q onto a convex set E, every P in E satisfies D(P||Q) ≥ D(P||P*) + D(P*||Q).

name: Large deviation theory
description: The study of exponential decay rates of probabilities of rare events, identifying the rate as a relative-entropy (or rate-function) minimization over the event.

name: Binary hypothesis testing problem
description: The decision problem of choosing between two candidate distributions P_1 and P_2 for observed data, with error probabilities of type I (alpha) and type II (beta).

name: Likelihood ratio test
description: The optimal test deciding between two hypotheses by comparing the ratio of their likelihoods to a threshold T.

name: Chernoff–Stein lemma
description: For fixed type I error bounded by epsilon, the best achievable exponent of the type II error is the relative entropy D(P_1||P_2), i.e. beta_n ≈ 2^{-nD(P_1||P_2)}.

name: Chernoff information
description: The quantity C(P_1,P_2) = -min_{0≤λ≤1} log Σ P_1^λ(x) P_2^{1-λ}(x), the best achievable exponent of the overall (Bayesian) probability of error in binary hypothesis testing.

name: Bayesian probability of error exponent
description: The minimal Bayesian probability of error in deciding between P_1 and P_2 from n i.i.d. samples decays with exponent equal to the Chernoff information C(P_1,P_2), independent of the priors.

name: Relative entropy and Fisher information (local approximation)
description: For nearby parameters, the relative entropy between f(·;θ) and f(·;θ+dθ) is to second order (1/2) J(θ) dθ^2, making Fisher information the local curvature of the KL divergence.

name: Score function
description: The derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the parameter, whose expectation is zero and whose variance is the Fisher information.

name: Maximum entropy principle
description: The principle of choosing, among all distributions satisfying given constraints, the one of maximum (differential) entropy as the least-biased model.

name: Maximum entropy distribution
description: The entropy-maximizing distribution under moment constraints, which has exponential-family form f*(x)=exp(λ_0+Σ λ_i r_i(x)) with multipliers fixing the moments.

name: Maximum entropy theorem
description: The distribution of exponential-family form matching given moment constraints uniquely maximizes differential entropy among all distributions meeting those constraints.

name: Burg's maximum entropy theorem
description: Among all stationary processes with prescribed autocorrelation values R_0,...,R_p, the one of maximum entropy rate is the p-th order Gauss–Markov (autoregressive) process matching those correlations.

name: Maximum entropy spectral estimation
description: The spectral density estimate obtained by maximizing entropy rate subject to known autocorrelations, yielding an all-pole (autoregressive) spectrum.

name: Existence of maximum entropy distribution
description: A maximum entropy distribution of the exponential form exists matching the constraints precisely when such an exponential-form distribution is normalizable and satisfies them; otherwise the supremum is not attained.

name: Universal source coding
type_signature: (unknown source class) → code achieving entropy rate
description: Lossless coding that asymptotically achieves the entropy rate of an unknown source drawn from a known class, without prior knowledge of the source statistics.

name: Minimax redundancy
description: The smallest worst-case excess of expected code length over entropy, minimized over codes and maximized over sources in the class, characterizing the price of universality.

name: Redundancy of a code
type_signature: (code, source θ) → expected length minus entropy
description: The expected per-symbol excess of a code's length over the source entropy, equal to the relative entropy between the true distribution and the coding distribution.

name: Lempel–Ziv (LZ78) coding
description: A universal compression algorithm that incrementally parses the input into distinct phrases, each the shortest new string, coded as a pointer to a previous phrase plus a new symbol.

name: Lempel–Ziv (LZ77) sliding-window coding
description: A universal compression algorithm that encodes the next text segment as a pointer (offset and match length) into a sliding window of recently seen text.

name: LZ78 phrase / dictionary tree
description: The dictionary of distinct phrases produced by incremental LZ78 parsing, whose count c(n) controls the codeword length.

name: Optimality of LZ78
description: For a stationary ergodic source, the compression rate of LZ78 converges almost surely to the entropy rate, making it asymptotically optimal without knowledge of the source.

name: Optimality of sliding-window (LZ77) coding
description: Sliding-window Lempel–Ziv compression achieves the entropy rate of a stationary ergodic source as the window size grows, using recurrence-time properties of the source.

name: Bound on number of distinct LZ phrases
description: The number c(n) of distinct phrases in the LZ78 parsing of a length-n string satisfies c(n) ≤ n/((1-ε_n) log n), the key combinatorial bound for proving optimality.

name: Kolmogorov complexity
description: The length of the shortest binary program that makes a universal computer output the string x and halt, the algorithmic measure of descriptive complexity.

name: Conditional Kolmogorov complexity
description: The length of the shortest program that outputs x given the string y (and its length) as additional input to the universal computer.

name: Universality (invariance) of Kolmogorov complexity
description: For any other computer A there is a constant c_A such that K_U(x) ≤ K_A(x) + c_A, so complexity relative to a universal machine is machine-independent up to an additive constant.

name: Upper bound on Kolmogorov complexity
description: For any string, K(x | ℓ(x)) ≤ ℓ(x) + c and K(x) ≤ ℓ(x) + 2 log ℓ(x) + c, so complexity is at most the length plus a small description of the length.

name: Kolmogorov complexity and entropy
description: For an i.i.d. source with entropy H, the expected Kolmogorov complexity per symbol of a length-n sequence converges to H, linking algorithmic and Shannon information.

name: Universal probability
description: The probability that a universal computer fed random program bits outputs x, dominating every computable distribution up to a multiplicative constant.

name: Universal probability ≈ 2^{-K(x)}
description: The universal probability of a string and its Kolmogorov complexity satisfy log(1/P_U(x)) = K(x) + O(1), so the most likely program is essentially the shortest one.

name: Incompressible sequence
description: A finite string whose Kolmogorov complexity is at least its length (no shorter description exists), of which most strings of each length are examples.

name: Algorithmically random (infinite) sequence
type_signature: infinite binary sequence with K(x_1..x_n) ≥ n - c
description: An infinite sequence all of whose prefixes are essentially incompressible, the algorithmic notion of randomness (Martin-Löf / Kolmogorov).

name: Chaitin's Omega
description: The halting probability of a universal prefix machine fed random bits, a well-defined real number that is algorithmically random and noncomputable.

name: Noncomputability of Kolmogorov complexity
description: There is no algorithm that computes K(x) for all strings x; the complexity function is uncomputable, related to the undecidability of the halting problem.

name: Kolmogorov sufficient statistic
type_signature: (string x) → finite set / model S* with x ∈ S*
description: The smallest finite-complexity description (model) S* containing x relative to which the remaining bits of x are random, separating structure from noise in a single string.

name: Kolmogorov structure function
type_signature: (x, complexity bound k) → log|S| over sets S∋x with K(S)≤k
description: The function giving, for each model-complexity budget k, the smallest log-cardinality of a set containing x describable in ≤ k bits, tracing the structure/randomness trade-off.

name: Occam's razor (algorithmic form)
description: The principle, justified by universal probability, that the shortest computable explanation consistent with the data should be preferred because it has the highest a priori probability.

name: Universal gambling scheme
description: A betting strategy that distributes wealth across all programs proportional to 2^{-ℓ(p)}, guaranteeing capital growth tied to the Kolmogorov complexity of the realized sequence.

name: Network information theory
description: The study of information flow in networks with multiple senders and receivers, characterizing achievable rate regions rather than single capacities.

name: Multiple-access channel (MAC)
description: A channel with several independent senders and one receiver, modeled by a single conditional distribution of the output given all the inputs.

name: Multiple-access channel capacity region
description: The set of achievable rate pairs (R_1,R_2) for the MAC, the closure of the convex hull of all rates satisfying R_1 ≤ I(X_1;Y|X_2), R_2 ≤ I(X_2;Y|X_1), and R_1+R_2 ≤ I(X_1,X_2;Y) for some product input distribution.

name: Gaussian multiple-access channel capacity
description: The capacity region of the Gaussian MAC with powers P_1,P_2 and noise N, given by R_i ≤ C(P_i/N) per user and R_1+R_2 ≤ C((P_1+P_2)/N) jointly, with C(x)=(1/2)log(1+x).

name: Successive cancellation (onion-peeling) decoding
description: A decoding strategy that decodes one user's message, subtracts its effect, and decodes the next, achieving corner points of the multiple-access capacity region.

name: Broadcast channel
description: A channel with one sender and several receivers, each receiving a possibly different output of a single transmitted signal.

name: Degraded broadcast channel
description: A broadcast channel in which the receivers can be ordered so that the worse receiver's output is a degraded (further-processed) version of the better receiver's output.

name: Capacity region of the degraded broadcast channel
description: The achievable rate region for a degraded broadcast channel, R_1 ≤ I(X;Y_1|U), R_2 ≤ I(U;Y_2), achieved by superposition coding over an auxiliary variable U.

name: Superposition coding
description: An encoding that superimposes a fine codeword for the strong receiver on a coarse cloud-center codeword for the weak receiver, achieving the degraded broadcast region.

name: Gaussian broadcast channel capacity
description: The capacity region of the degraded Gaussian broadcast channel, obtained by splitting power αP and (1−α)P between the two users with superposition coding.

name: Slepian–Wolf rate region
description: The achievable rate region for separate lossless encoding of correlated sources, the pentagon defined by R_1 ≥ H(X|Y), R_2 ≥ H(Y|X), R_1+R_2 ≥ H(X,Y).

name: Transmission of correlated sources over a MAC
description: A sufficient condition for sending correlated sources over a multiple-access channel, in which the source correlation can be exploited and source–channel separation generally fails.

name: Relay channel
description: A channel with a sender, a receiver, and an intermediate relay node that helps convey the message by transmitting based on its own received signal.

name: Capacity of the degraded relay channel
description: The capacity of a degraded relay channel, C = max min{I(X,X_1;Y), I(X;Y_1|X_1)}, achieved by block-Markov decode-and-forward coding.

name: Interference channel
description: A channel with two sender–receiver pairs in which each receiver wants only its own sender's message while suffering interference from the other transmission.

name: Capacity of the strong-interference Gaussian interference channel
description: For strong interference, the Gaussian interference channel capacity region coincides with that of the corresponding compound multiple-access channel, since each receiver can decode both messages.

name: Gelfand–Pinsker theorem (channel with side information)
description: The capacity of a channel with state known noncausally at the encoder is C = max [I(U;Y) − I(U;S)] over auxiliary U and encoding x(u,s).

name: Writing on dirty paper (Costa)
description: For a Gaussian channel with additive Gaussian interference known at the transmitter, the capacity equals that of the interference-free channel, so the known interference costs nothing.

name: Gelfand–Pinsker binning
function_signature: (message, known state) → codeword via auxiliary bins
description: An encoding that organizes auxiliary codewords into bins per message and chooses within a bin one jointly typical with the known state, the dual of Slepian–Wolf binning.

name: Failure of source–channel separation in networks
description: Unlike the point-to-point case, separately optimal source coding and channel coding are not in general optimal for networks, as exhibited by correlated sources over a MAC.

name: Gaussian multiuser channels
description: The family of additive white Gaussian noise network models (MAC, broadcast, relay, interference) used to obtain explicit multiuser capacity regions.

name: Stock market (price relative vector)
description: A model of m stocks given by a random vector X of price relatives, where X_i is the ratio of end-of-day to start-of-day price of stock i.

name: Portfolio
description: An allocation of wealth across stocks given by a probability vector b, where b_i is the fraction invested in stock i.

name: Doubling rate
type_signature: (portfolio b, distribution F) → W(b,F) = E[log b^T X]
description: The expected logarithm of the wealth relative b^T X of a portfolio, the exponential growth rate of wealth under repeated reinvestment.

name: Log-optimal portfolio
description: The portfolio b* maximizing the expected log wealth (doubling rate), which maximizes the long-run growth rate of capital.

name: Kuhn–Tucker characterization of the log-optimal portfolio
description: A portfolio b* is log-optimal iff E[X_i / (b*^T X)] ≤ 1 for every stock, with equality for every stock held with positive weight.

name: Competitive optimality of the log-optimal portfolio
description: For the log-optimal portfolio b* and any other portfolio b, the probability that b does at least as well as b* by a factor t is at most 1/t, so b* is competitively optimal.

name: Expected-ratio bound for log-optimal wealth
description: For the log-optimal portfolio b* and any portfolio b, E[(b^T X)/(b*^T X)] ≤ 1, the key inequality underlying competitive optimality.

name: Side information increases growth rate by mutual information
description: The increase in the optimal doubling rate of a stock market due to side information Y is at most the mutual information I(X;Y) between the market and the side information.

name: Asymptotic optimality of log-optimal investment (AEP for investment)
description: For a stationary ergodic market, the wealth of the log-optimal (causal) portfolio strategy grows to first order in the exponent like 2^{nW*}, and no causal strategy does better.

name: Universal portfolio
description: Cover's causal investment strategy that performs a wealth-weighted average over all constant-rebalanced portfolios, achieving the same exponential growth as the best constant portfolio chosen in hindsight.

name: Constant rebalanced portfolio
description: An investment strategy that rebalances to the same fixed proportion vector b every trading period regardless of past prices.

name: Asymptotic optimality of the universal portfolio
description: The universal portfolio's wealth is within a polynomial factor of the best constant rebalanced portfolio in hindsight, so it achieves the same growth-rate exponent without knowing the future.

name: Entropy power
description: The variance of a Gaussian having the same differential entropy per dimension as X, the quantity through which entropy and second-moment inequalities connect.

name: Entropy power inequality (EPI)
description: For independent random vectors X and Y, the entropy power of the sum dominates the sum of entropy powers: 2^{(2/n)h(X+Y)} ≥ 2^{(2/n)h(X)} + 2^{(2/n)h(Y)}.

name: Fisher information (of a random vector under translation)
description: The translation Fisher information of a random vector, the expected squared gradient of its log density, central to the Fisher information and entropy-power chain.

name: Fisher information inequality
description: For independent random vectors X and Y, the reciprocal Fisher information is superadditive: 1/J(X+Y) ≥ 1/J(X) + 1/J(Y).

name: Cramér–Rao (estimation form) via Fisher information
description: The Fisher information of a random variable is at least the reciprocal of its variance, J(X) ≥ 1/var(X), with equality for the Gaussian.

name: de Bruijn's identity
description: The rate of change of the differential entropy of X + √t Z (Z standard Gaussian) with respect to t equals half the Fisher information: (d/dt) h(X+√t Z) = (1/2) J(X+√t Z).

name: Minkowski determinant inequality
description: For positive-definite K_1 and K_2, |K_1+K_2|^{1/n} ≥ |K_1|^{1/n} + |K_2|^{1/n}, the determinant analogue of the entropy power inequality.

name: Szász's inequality
description: A chain of inequalities relating the determinant of a positive-definite matrix to the geometric means of the determinants of its principal submatrices of each order, following from subset-entropy inequalities.

name: Han's inequality (subset entropy inequality)
description: The average of the entropies of all size-k subsets of a set of random variables, normalized by k, is nonincreasing in k, so larger subsets give smaller per-variable entropy.

name: Han's inequality for relative entropies
description: The analogue of Han's inequality for relative entropy, in which averaged subset relative entropies are monotone, used to derive determinant inequalities for ratios of distributions.

name: Subset inequalities for determinants
description: A family of inequalities, generalizing Hadamard and Szász, bounding the determinant of a covariance matrix by symmetric functions of the determinants of its principal submatrices.

name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality (covariance form)
description: For random variables with finite second moments, (E[XY])^2 ≤ E[X^2]E[Y^2], used to bound covariances and underlie the Cramér–Rao bound.
